cases.customer_question: Can I convert a dual-mode Bluetooth module into a BLE-only qualification without additional testing?
question_variants: Can I change dual mode QDID to BLE only without tests?
Is it possible to register a dual-mode module as BLE only?
Do I need testing to convert BR/EDR+LE to LE-only?
Can I disable BR/EDR and claim LE-only qualification?
Does QPRD allow editing transport modes without testing?
cases.actual_issue: Restrictions in QPRD preventing conversion of dual-mode designs to single-mode without additional testing due to stricter host-controller consistency checks.
cases.plain_english_explanation: A Bluetooth module that supports both Classic and LE cannot simply be declared as LE-only during certification. Even if you disable Classic features in software, the official certification still considers the original capabilities unless extra testing is done.
cases.consultant_answer: Under the post-2024 qualification rules, host and controller layers must be consistent. A dual-mode controller cannot be re-declared as LE-only without additional testing. However, if BR/EDR is disabled at runtime via firmware but still present in the implementation, the product can remain registered as dual-mode without requiring additional protocol testing such as L2CAP/GAP for LE-only conversion.
cases.decision_logic: Transport mode (LE vs BR/EDR vs dual) must match across layers; changing declared mode requires new testing unless the original design is preserved.
cases.final_recommendation: Keep the qualification as dual-mode and disable BR/EDR in firmware for product behavior, unless you are prepared to perform additional protocol testing for LE-only registration.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Attempting to declare LE-only without proper testing may cause qualification rejection due to layer inconsistency or missing required test evidence.
